key_gap: Both sides staged the portfolio with identical EV arithmetic (staged 108.8 vs all-in 89.5, +€19M; year-1 €7M vs €80M — staging is also the only budget-feasible structure) and pre-committed kill criteria, but the human's structure is a decision instrument while the AI's is a correct generic stage-gate plan. The human calibrated kill thresholds against payoff mix (conditional success ≤ 20% with payoff < €300M → kill), designed each gate's readout to test the project's dominant failure mode so pass/fail shifts the continuation decision, and read project C as a quasi-option — a funded C has no further decision branch, so it is a lottery ticket whose gate-1 kill trigger should fire eagerly — whereas the AI applied a blanket 15% conditional-success floor, treated gates as generic milestones, and left C's no-branch structure and redeployment triggers unexamined until REVIEW.
learning_signal: For stage-gated R&D portfolios, EV arithmetic is the floor, not the skill: a gate is worth only its decision-relevant information. (1) Kill criteria must be calibrated to payoff mix, not blanket probability floors; (2) each gate's readout must test the project's dominant failure mode, else pass/fail cannot shift the continuation decision and the gate is theater; (3) projects whose funded outcome is terminal have no compound structure — they are lottery tickets with exactly one real decision point, to be held only while capital is free and killed first on redeployment; (4) the redeployment of killed capital is part of the option value — freed Stage-2 funds return to the pool and winners get priority with explicit triggers.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'gate-value audit' in HOW for every proposed stage gate: require (a) the decision it feeds, (b) the readout that would shift that decision (test the dominant failure mode), and (c) confirmation of a genuine exercise branch at the gate (compound vs terminal structure — a terminal outcome is a lottery ticket, not an option). Calibrate kill thresholds against payoff magnitude rather than blanket floors, and make the redeployment rule trigger-prioritized (winners-first at the next gate) instead of descriptive.

key_gap: The pure style validated its registry-documented failure mode in full: it accepted the CEO's 'test chip buys information' premise, priced the option from fabricated probabilities (75% validate / 80% conditional win → staged EV $58.5M vs all-in $54.5M), compressed a 25-month critical path (6+7+12) to '≈18' by asserting an RTL/qualification overlap that the design-freeze requirement forbids, and never asked whether the option could be exercised in time or at all — the window closes at T+18, the readout covers yield and a simplified core while the real risk is architecture-level qualification behavior with zero base rates (posterior ≈ prior), and no exercise alternative exists because the program is the company's only revenue path (abandonment value = 0; 'capped downside' is fiction). The AI diagnosed pre-EV: calendar check (25 > 18 → staging misses by 7 months even best-case), information audit (readout not decision-relevant), exercise-alternative audit (fake option), then selected full-speed commitment with the probe run in parallel as priced manufacturing-risk data, spend phased by contract milestones, and design margins as insurance.
learning_signal: Before any option EV is computed, audit the three pre-conditions of option value: (1) calendar — can the option be exercised before it expires (critical-path check; a stage gate that consumes the window destroys value regardless of EV); (2) information — would the readout actually shift the decision (surrogate relevance vs the real risk; base-rate existence — with none, posterior ≈ prior and any p is fabricated); (3) exercise alternative — does a genuine abandon/continue branch exist (no exit ⇒ fake option). When any pre-condition fails, stage the money, not the clock: commit at full speed with spend phaseing (milestones) and downside insurance (margins, second-sourcing), and treat 'buy information cheaply' as a hypothesis to verify, not a premise to accept.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'fake-option check' to the WHY stage for any staging proposal: (a) run the critical-path calendar before any EV; (b) audit the planned readout for decision relevance and base rates (would a pass change the decision? is any p defensible?); (c) verify a real exercise alternative exists. If any audit fails, switch to commit-with-phaseing and state why the staged EV is arithmetic theater rather than value. Also add a WHAT-level rule: for time-critical commitments, treat the deadline as a constraint that frames the deliverable, not as background.
